A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block.
A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell.
A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code one 40-character screen row below the first cell.
A 256-byte table of bottom-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D60 writes the selected code one row below and one cell to the right of the first cell.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy bytes at $AE58,Y and $AE59,Y into the operand of the JSR at $A8D9. Controlled inputs 0–23 select the captured pointer pairs; no local index bound is enforced. The target routines and natural-play contexts remain open.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy bytes at $AE58,Y and $AE59,Y into the operand of the JSR at $A8F1. Controlled inputs 0–23 select the captured pointer pairs; no local index bound is enforced. The target routines and natural-play contexts remain open.

Store 0 in the shop mode byte at $AB00, store $DC in the countdown at $AB04, and fall through to the wait path at $A940. Starting from 0, the captured left and right handlers keep the mode among $FF, $00 and $01 if no other code changes it; ordinary-play timing and other possible writes remain open.

Call $3C2A, decrement the shop countdown at $AB04 and branch to $A973 when it becomes zero. Otherwise call $370B, $AA77 and $AA64; on set carry, repeat this path. On clear carry, fall through to $A953. Starting from the initialized $DC and holding the tested branches, zero is reached after 220 calls to $3C2A; the duration in seconds is not established.

Call $3C2A, decrement $AB04 and branch to $A973 at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $AA77 and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $A964. The controlled test stubs these calls; normal-play timing and other exits remain open.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $A9C7; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $A989; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $A9A7. When all three are nonzero, jump back to $A953. The preceding code calls $3C4C to sample joystick port 2; fire takes priority over left, and left over right.

If $AAFF is nonzero, jump to $A86A. Otherwise load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X, load X/Y with message pointer $AB41, and jump to the $77E0 call at $AA40. The selector used by $77E0 and natural timeout reachability remain open.

If the signed mode byte at $AB00 is negative, return to the wait path at $A940. Otherwise decrement it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $AAFF is zero, pass the item index at $AB05 to the message selector at $AA8F. Call $AA77 and return to the wait path. The mode’s possible ordinary-play values remain open.

If the mode byte at $AB00 equals 1, return to the wait path at $A940. Otherwise increment it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $AAFF is zero, pass the item index at $AB06 to the message selector at $AA8F. Call $AA77 and return to the wait path. The mode’s possible ordinary-play values remain open.

Read $AAFF; if nonzero, load $AB00 and jump to $A7E3. Otherwise load X from $7B and read $AB00. If nonzero, branch to the purchase index choice at $A9F0, preserving the negative flag from that read. If zero, inspect $4753,X: a negative value or a clear bit 1 selects message pointer $AB69; a nonnegative value with bit 1 set selects $AB52. Both paths jump to the $77E0 message call. The meanings and ordinary-play ranges of the two gate bytes remain open.

Choose an item index using the incoming negative flag: load $AB05 when it is set, or $AB06 when clear, then enter the price selector at $A9FB. The path at $A9C7 supplies that flag from $AB00; other entries remain open.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts, use the result as Y, and copy the two bytes at $AE56,Y and $AE57,Y to $7D/$7E. Call $7901, which subtracts the packed-decimal amount from the selected player’s gold, restores it on insufficient funds, returns carry set on success and clears decimal mode. Inputs 0–23 were checked; no local index bound is enforced.

After the $7901 price subtraction, jump to $A940 on clear carry. On set carry, load X from $7B and decrement $4753,X with eight-bit wrap. Read $AB00; if negative select the item index at $AB05, otherwise select $AB06. Push it and continue to the offset-4 routine-pointer selector at $AA25. The natural contexts and callback effects remain open.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy bytes at $AE5A,Y and $AE5B,Y into the operand of the JSR at $AA39. Controlled inputs 0–23 select the captured pointer pairs; no local index bound is enforced. The target routines and natural-play contexts remain open.

Pull the selected item index, clear carry, add 1 in binary mode and call the JSR whose operand was patched by the selector. Load X/Y with $AB2E and call $77E0, then call $3C2A and $370B repeatedly while $4D6B is nonzero. Return once it is zero. The effect, message and waiting callbacks were stubbed in controlled tests; this does not establish ordinary-play reachability.
Load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X and return. Several item-effect routines tail-call this helper.

Multiply A by 8 using three eight-bit shifts, clear carry, add 6 and use the eight-bit result as X. Read the high byte from $AE57,X into Y and the low byte from $AE56,X into X, then jump to $77E0. Inputs 0–23 select the captured item-message pointers; the arithmetic aliases inputs modulo 32 and there is no local bound check. The message routine uses this X/Y pointer when its selector $77E1 is zero.
